newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-SOUTH AFRICA TAKE CONTROL OF SECOND TEST.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SOUTH AFRICA TAKE CONTROL OF SECOND TEST.

text.p: A spectacular Australian collapse and positive South African batting put the hosts in complete control on the second day of the second test in Port Elizabeth on Saturday.

With three days remaining, South Africa have a lead of 184 with all ten wickets remaining after dismissing Australia for a meagre 108 -- for a first innings lead of 101 -- and then reaching 83 without loss by the close in their second innings.

Resuming at 10 for one in the morning, Australia lost captain Mark Taylor in the third over of the morning for eight to carry his miserable run of form to 17 consecutive test innings without a half century.

But the wicket was a bitter-sweet success for South Africa as the successful bowler, Shaun Pollock, then had to limp off with a strained left hamstring after bowling just two overs. He will not be able to bowl again in the test.

Mark Waugh briefly flattered to deceive in a 36 ball innings of 20 that included three typically elegant boundaries. but he became the third wicket to fall when a Hansie Cronje in-swinger trapped him leg before wicket with the total on 48.
Just 49 runs were scored in the morning session as Australia's suspicion of a well grassed but far from impossible wicket led them into a shotless, defensive bunker.
After lunching at 59 for three, the afternoon disaster began when Steve Waugh sent batting partner Matthew Elliott back after initially responding to a call for a sharp single.
Hansie Cronje quickly recovered from a slight fumble and Elliott was run out for a marathon 23 from 120 deliveries in nearly three hours.

Steve Waugh, who said before the test that "Australia just can't lose..." then edged all rounder Brian McMillan to keeper Dave Richardson who took a spectacular one handed diving catch in front of slip. Waugh made eight.
Panic seemed to set in as Michael Bevan glanced McMillan down the leg side only to see Richardson's gloves once again waiting to accept the offering. Bevan posted the sixth duck of the match.
Ian Healy (5) then made a mess of a hook shot and lobbed a simple catch to square leg and Greg Blewett (13) lost his off stump to an off-cutter from Allan Donald after batting for 81 minutes.
Shane Warne contributed a brace of lusty boundaries in his 18 but Australia were beyond rescue.

When South Africa batted a second time they adopted an approach in complete contrast to the Australians. Gary Kirsten and Adam Bacher attacked at the slightest opportunity, driving, hooking and cutting wherever possible.
By the close of play Kirsten was unbeaten on 41 with Bacher on 38. To compound a miserable day for Australia, Steve Waugh limped off the field half way through his fifth over with a groin strain.
